lexemes.gloss: Toward the center, source, or main point of reference; toward the end at which something is attached.
examples: The information made its way up the chain of command to the general.
I felt something crawling up my arm.

lexemes.gloss: From south to north of.
examples: We sailed up the East Coast of England from Ipswich to South Shields.

lexemes.gloss: From the mouth towards the source of (a river or waterway).
examples: He led an expedition up the Amazon.

lexemes.gloss: Of a person: having sex with.
examples: Phwoar, look at that bird. I'd love to be up her.

lexemes.gloss: At (a given place, especially one imagined to be higher or more distant from a central location).
examples: I'll see you later up the snooker club.

lexemes.gloss: Facing upwards.
examples: Turn the cloth over so that the patterned side is up.

lexemes.gloss: On or at a physically higher level.
examples: The flood waters are up again across large areas of the country.

lexemes.gloss: Headed or designated to go upward (as an escalator, stairway, elevator etc.) or toward (as a run-up).
examples: Where is the up escalator?

lexemes.gloss: Fitted or fixed at a high or relatively high position, especially on a wall or ceiling.
examples: All the notices are up now.
The Christmas decorations are up.

lexemes.gloss: Available to view or use; made public; posted.
examples: Is your new video up yet? I looked on the website, but I couldn't find it.

lexemes.gloss: Aloft.
examples: The kite is up!

lexemes.gloss: Raised; lifted.
examples: The castle drawbridge was up.
Don't go into the living room just now – I've got the carpet up.

lexemes.gloss: Of a river, in flood or at a high level.
Built, constructed.
examples: Are the new buildings up yet?

lexemes.gloss: Standing; upright.
examples: The audience were up and on their feet.

lexemes.gloss: Awake and out of bed.
examples: I can’t believe it’s 3 a.m. and you’re still up.

lexemes.gloss: Riding the horse; mounted.
Above the horizon, in the sky.
examples: It'll get warmer once the sun's up.

lexemes.gloss: Larger; greater in quantity, volume, value etc.
examples: Sales are up compared to last quarter.
My temperature is up this morning.

lexemes.gloss: Indicating a larger or higher quantity.
examples: The barometer is up, so fine weather should be on the way.

lexemes.gloss: Ahead; leading; winning.
examples: The home team were up by two goals at half-time.

lexemes.gloss: Finished, at an end.
examples: Time is up!
Her contract is up next month, so it's time to negotiate another one.

lexemes.gloss: In a good mood.
examples: I’m feeling up today.

lexemes.gloss: Willing; ready.
examples: If you are up for a trip, let’s go.

lexemes.gloss: Next in a sequence.
examples: Smith is up to bat.

lexemes.gloss: Happening; new; of concern. See also what's up, what's up with.
examples: What's up, bro?
What is up with that project at headquarters?
When I saw his face, I knew something was up.

lexemes.gloss: Said of the higher-ranking pair in a two pair.
examples: AAKK = aces up
QQ33 = queens up

lexemes.gloss: Well-informed; current.
examples: I’m not up on the latest news. What’s going on?

lexemes.gloss: Functional; working.
examples: Is the server back up?

lexemes.gloss: Traveling towards a major terminus.
examples: The London train is on the up line.

lexemes.gloss: Chilled and served without ice; (often specifically) shaken with ice and then strained into a coupe for serving, leaving the ice behind.
examples: Would you like that drink up or on ice?

lexemes.gloss: Risen up, rebelling, in revolt.
Erect.
At university (especially Oxford or Cambridge).
Well-known; renowned.
The direction opposed to the pull of gravity.
examples: Up is a good way to go.

lexemes.gloss: A positive thing, or a time or situation when things are going well.
examples: I hate almost everything about my job. The only up is that it's so close to home.
There are many ups to caravanning, but also many downs.
I've been on an up all this week.

lexemes.gloss: An up quark.
An upstairs room of a two story house.
examples: She lives in a two-up two-down.

lexemes.gloss: To physically raise or lift.
examples: We upped anchor and sailed away.

lexemes.gloss: To rise to a standing position; hence, by extension, to act suddenly; see also up and.
examples: She was sitting there quietly, then all of a sudden she upped and left.
He just upped and quit.
He upped and punched that guy.

lexemes.gloss: To increase the level or amount of.
examples: If we up the volume, we may be able to hear what he says.
As usual, they've upped the prices for Valentine's Day.
My psychiatrist upped my guanfacine dose since ADHD symptoms have not gotten better.

lexemes.gloss: To promote.
examples: It wasn’t long before they upped him to Vice President.

lexemes.gloss: To ascend; to climb up.
To upload.
examples: 100 new apps and games have just been upped.
